scope: Proposition 7.1 (Matched-clock rate transfer) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For almost every point (i, u) of the characteristic plane with i > 0 and 0 < u < 1, put s = S′(u). There is a constant σ > 0, depending only on the matched process and m, for which 0 < s ≤ 1 and the following assertions hold. 1. If m ̸= 1, each of the chains x −→ y and w −→ z has the rule d > 0 =⇒ e ≥ min(1, d + s), where d, e are its source and target rates. Each of x −→ w and y −→ z has the same rule with σ in place of s. 2. If m = 1, then x > 0 =⇒ q ≥ s, x > 0, z < 1 =⇒ z ≥ x + s, z < 1 =⇒ q ≤ 2 − s. The bounds include 0 ≤ x, y, w, z ≤ 1, or 0 ≤ q ≤ 2 in the tied case, supplied by the coordinate capacities.
